content: 1. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of nimodipine by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 2. Nirmatrelvir increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor for increased adverse effects of erythromycin, including QTc interval prolongation. 3. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for erythromycin-related adverse effects, including QTc prolongation. 4. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of nitrendipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of norgestrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic concentrations of norgestrel, raising the risk of adverse effects. Use caution and monitor. 6. Erythromycin lactobionate and ofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. 7. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of oliceridine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration is necessary, reduce the frequency of oliceridine dosing, monitor for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust subsequent doses accordingly. If the inhibitor is discontinued, consider increasing the oliceridine dosage until stable drug effects are achieved. Monitor for signs of opioid withdrawal. 8. Erythromycin lactobionate and olodaterol inhaled both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. Drugs that prolong the QTc interval may potentiate the cardiovascular effects of beta-2 agonists, increasing the risk of ventricular arrhythmias. 9. Erythromycin lactobionate and osilodrostat both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 10. Erythromycin lactobionate and osimertinib both prolong the QTc interval. Conduct periodic monitoring with ECGs and electrolytes in patients taking drugs known to prolong the QTc interval. 11. Oxaliplatin increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate through an unknown mechanism. Monitor for ECG changes if therapy is initiated in patients taking drugs known to prolong the QT interval. 12. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of oxybutynin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 13. Erythromycin lactobionate and ozanimod both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. Due to potential additive effects on heart rate, ozanimod treatment should generally not be initiated in patients concurrently treated with QT-prolonging drugs with known arrhythmogenic properties. 14. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of paclitaxel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 15. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of palbociclib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 16. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of paliperidone by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Both erythromycin lactobionate and paliperidone prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. 17. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of palovarotene by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration of palovarotene with moderate CYP3A inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the palovarotene dose by 50%. 18. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the levels or effects of pantothenic acid by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. 19. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of parecoxib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 20. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of paromomycin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 21. Erythromycin lactobionate and paroxetine both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. 22. Erythromycin lactobionate and pasireotide both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. 23. Erythromycin lactobionate and pazopanib both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 24. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of pimozide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 25. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of pioglitazone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 26. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the effects of piperacillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. Use caution and monitor. 27. Ponatinib increases the levels of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 28. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of posaconazole by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Both erythromycin lactobionate and posaconazole prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. 29. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the toxicity of pravastatin through an OATP1B1 inhibition mechanism, which may increase the risk of myopathy. Use caution and monitor. 30. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of prednisolone by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 31. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of prednisone by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 32. Pretomanid increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate through an unknown mechanism. Increase monitoring for drug-related adverse effects if pretomanid is co-administered with sensitive OATP1B3 substrates. 33. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of propafenone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 34. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the levels or effects of pyridoxine by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. 35. Erythromycin lactobionate and quetiapine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid use with drugs that prolong QT and in patients with risk factors for prolonged QT interval. Postmarketing cases show QT prolongation with overdose in patients with concomitant illness or with drugs known to cause electrolyte imbalance or prolong QT. 36. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of quinine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both erythromycin lactobionate and quinine prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 37. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of ramelteon by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 38. Erythromycin lactobionate and ranolazine both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. 39. Ribociclib increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 40. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels of rifaximin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 41. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels of rilpivirine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of erythromycin lactobionate by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. Rilpivirine should be used cautiously when co-administered with a drug with a known risk of Torsades de Pointes. 42. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of rimegepant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid repeating the rimegepant dose within 48 hours if co-administered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor. 43. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of risperidone by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Both erythromycin lactobionate and risperidone prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. 44. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 45. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels of rivaroxaban by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Patients with renal impairment receiving rivaroxaban with drugs that are combined P-gp and weak or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may have significant increases in exposure compared with patients with normal renal function and no inhibitor use. Since these increases may raise bleeding risk, use rivaroxaban in this situation only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk. 46. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels of roflumilast by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with dual inhibitors of CYP3A4 and CYP1A2 may increase systemic exposure and result in increased adverse reactions. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. 47. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of romidepsin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Both erythromycin lactobionate and romidepsin prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. 48. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the toxicity of rosuvastatin through an OATP1B1 inhibition mechanism, which may increase the risk of myopathy. Use caution and monitor. 49. Rucaparib increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the dosage of CYP3A4 substrates if clinically indicated. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. 50. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of ruxolitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 51. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of sacubitril/valsartan through an unknown mechanism. Co-administration with OATP1B1 inhibitors may increase valsartan systemic exposure. Use caution and monitor. 52. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of saxagliptin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 53. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels of seladelpar by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised in patients who are poor CYP2C9 metabolizers taking seladelpar and are co-administered a moderate/strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 54. Selpercatinib increases the toxicity of erythromycin lactobionate by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 55. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of sildenafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider a starting dose of 25 mg in patients treated with erythromycin. 56. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of silodosin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 57. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of sirolimus by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 58. Sodium bicarbonate increases the levels of erythromycin lactobionate through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor. 59. Sodium citrate/citric acid increases the levels of erythromycin lactobionate through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor. 60. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the effects of sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid by altering metabolism. Co-administration with antibiotics decreases efficacy by altering colonic bacterial flora needed to convert sodium picosulfate to its active form. Use caution and monitor. 61. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of sonidegib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration of sonidegib with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. If a moderate CYP3A inhibitor must be used, administer it for less than 14 days and monitor closely for adverse reactions, particularly musculoskeletal adverse reactions. 62. Erythromycin lactobionate and sorafenib both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 63. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of sparsentan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. No dosage adjustment is needed. Monitor blood pressure, serum potassium, edema, and kidney function regularly if sparsentan is co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 64. Stiripentol increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Stiripentol is both a CYP3A4 inhibitor and inducer. Monitor CYP3A4 substrates co-administered with stiripentol for increased or decreased effects. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. Consider reducing the dose of P-glycoprotein substrates if adverse reactions are experienced when administered concomitantly.
